subject: LangFlow connector integration - tracing & SDK compatibility
messages:
From: Amit Gupta <amit@langflow.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: partnerships@langflow.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: LangFlow + Redwood: connector & tracing integration

Hi Karthik,

I lead partnerships at LangFlow — we build a visual low-code flow editor that a lot of ISVs embed into their products. We’ve heard good things about Redwood’s tracing hooks and SDKs from mutual customers and think there’s a clear opportunity for a certified connector that preserves token attribution and passes trace metadata end-to-end (LangFlow -> customer runtime -> Redwood).

High-level asks:
- Confirm whether Redwood can surface the tracing headers LangFlow emits (x-trace-id, x-span) and whether there’s an official SDK shim we should depend on.
- Any constraints around embedding Redwood’s runtime in LangFlow-managed sessions (SSO, KMS, and data retention concerns).
- A rough rubric for certifying a connector (security checklist + perf targets).

I attached a one-pager with our proposed data shape and a sample trace payload (langflow-integration-specs.pdf). Would you be open to a 30-min technical sync next week?

Best,
Amit Gupta
Head of Partnerships | LangFlow
attachments: langflow-integration-specs.pdf

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Gupta <amit@langflow.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LangFlow + Redwood: connector & tracing integration

Hi Amit — thanks for the note and the spec. I’ve looped in Vanessa (partnerships/PD) and Marissa (ISV integrations) so we can scope this quickly. A couple quick answers up-front:

- Tracing: Redwood preserves inbound trace headers and surface them in our Console. We also provide a lightweight SDK shim for client-side propagation; the runtime supports passthrough of x-trace-id and related fields. We’ll need to align on exact header names to avoid collisions.
- Embedding/runtime: Embedding LangFlow flows that call our hosted API is straightforward. If you expect customers to run a private deployment that proxies through LangFlow, we’ll need to discuss KMS/SSO patterns — the Private product supports customer-managed KMS and a VPC option.
- Cert rubric: Marissa can share a short checklist (security, perf, trace fidelity, retry/backoff behavior). Our perf target for a connector certification is mean p95 token latency <= 250ms for 512-token requests under expected load profile.

We’re available Tue/Wed next week for a 30-min deep dive. Proposed slots: Tue 10:00-10:30 PT or Wed 14:00-14:30 PT. Which works?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference
attachments: (none)

From: Amit Gupta <amit@langflow.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: partnerships@langflow.ai
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LangFlow + Redwood: connector & tracing integration

Karthik — thanks, that’s helpful. Tue 10:00 PT works for our engineers.

Quick answers to your checklist items so Marissa has something to review before the call:
- Header names: we currently emit x-langflow-trace-id and x-langflow-span; happy to alias to x-trace-id if that’s simpler on your side.
- SSO/KMS: many of our enterprise customers prefer an integration where LangFlow orchestrates flows but tokens are minted by the downstream vendor (your hosted API) via customer-specific credentials. We can support a proxy mode or a pass-through depending on the compliance profile.
- Perf: we see median response times of ~120ms for 256-token calls in our staging environment; can share a p95 trace sample during the call.

I’ve attached a draft SOW that outlines scope, milestone-based deliverables, and an initial co-marketing plan (langflow-sow-draft.docx).

See you Tue.

— Amit
attachments: langflow-sow-draft.docx

2) Vanessa — want to align on commercial motion. Suggested initial approach: connector certification (no revenue share) + optional co-sell for enterprise deals. Any objections?
